findings.note: L87-112: the round-1 budget fix holds only when a screen has 8 or fewer 1-hop destinations. listedHop1 holds only the 8 listed screens, so edges to the other 1-hop screens stay as affordances (up to topN=6), and the action text is not cut to 40 characters. A probe of buildSummary/renderSummary with 16 one-hop destinations gave 6 affordances, 8 reachable lines, 1111 chars and about 278 tokens, which is over the 200 that the docs and the L362 test claim. Fix: when the reachable list is present, leave out an affordance to any 1-hop screen (listed or not), or cap affordances (for example 3) and cut the action text. Add the 16-destination case to the token test.
findings.cause: The affordance filter uses the capped reachable list as the set of covered destinations, and the token test fixture (exactly 8 one-hop destinations plus a self-loop) never goes past the cap.

findings.note: L1117-1123: finalCompact returns node.compact when the stateHash matches, and the same applies to resolveCompactTier in describe-tiers.ts L202. A volatile node is persisted with compact "" but keeps its stateHash (store.ts L657-662), and hydrate (L704-723) keeps both. After a tool-server restart, a quiet landing whose stateHash repeats (up to 25% of visits on a volatile node) therefore returns `compact: ""` with no read. Fix: require `node.compact !== ""` in both cache checks, or delete stateHash in the volatile persist branch the same way the redacted branch does. Test: bounded store, volatile node, flush and load, landing at the same stateHash, and expect one getState and a non-empty compact.
findings.cause: The cache rule pairs stateHash with compact, but the volatile persist path breaks the pair by dropping compact while it keeps stateHash.

findings.note: L1115-1125: the landing cache copies the cache condition of resolveCompactTier instead of calling it. The parity test (test/screen-graph-navigate-targets.test.ts L300-313) runs against the real describeAndroidTiered, but only on the refresh path (the INTERNET node has no stateHash). The cache path is tested only with a literal (L259-268). Suggestion: route the landing case through resolveCompactTier with a lazy getState in refresh, so there is one rule, and add a parity case where describe also serves from the cache.

L101-103: removing an affordance whose destination is listed at 1 hop drops the action (which element to tap) and the success count for that screen. That is fine for navigate-to by label, but an agent that drives gesture-tap by hand, or that falls back after a divergence, no longer sees the tap target. The count is not actionable. Optional: put the action in the 1-hop reachable line when the budget allows, for example `(1 hop, tap "Network & internet")`.

L287-304: this round-1 note is still open. reachableScreens uses BFS hops over non-template edges and sorts ties by label, but navigate-to plans with a weighted Dijkstra, so the reply `hops`/`path` can differ from the `(N hops)` in the summary. Within the cap of 8, alphabetical ties can also push out the most used 1-hop screens. Not verifiable from the diff whether this matters on real graphs.
